title: Pre-Clinical Models of Infectious Diseases
description: Pre-solicitation Notice Information Introduction The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) supports research related to the basic understanding of microbiology and immunology leading to the development of vaccines, therapeutics, and medical diagnostics for the prevention, treatment, and diagnosis of infectious and immune-mediated diseases. The NIAID, Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases has a requirement to provide and develop animal models in order to advance our understanding of infectious diseases as well as advance the development of therapeutics and vaccines for infectious diseases. Description The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) supports and facilitates research that focuses on understanding, treating and, ultimately, preventing infectious, immunologic, and allergenic diseases. The NIAID Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) supports and facilitates research to understand, control and prevent human disease caused by infectious agents. Basic, applied and translational research to develop and assess therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics is supported through research grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts. In turn, DMID further supports and facilitates research ongoing under these funding mechanisms and through other programs via an array of preclinical and clinical resources and services to support multiples stages of the product development pipeline. These resources and services include genomic and gene sequencing services, provision of high quality biological materials, biocontainment facilities, and pre-clinical and clinical translational research resources (https://www.niaid.nih.gov/research/resources). The current NIAID Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program is one of DMID�s preclinical services resources and supports the development and refinement of animal models and animal replacement models of infectious diseases, models that subsequently are used to evaluate candidate medical countermeasures against these diseases. In addition, these contracts facilitate regulatory submissions, patents, and other intellectual property applications by extramural investigators who request evaluation of their products. This program serves the DMID mission of supporting investigator-initiated research by providing critical data needed to apply for grant or other funding. Finally, these contracts enable product developers and sponsors to make key go/no-go decisions for candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics. In addition to meeting the needs of extramural researchers, this program provides crucial data to our DHHS agency partners. These data will facilitate the advancement of promising candidate medical countermeasures against priority biodefense and emerging infectious agents to approval or licensure, and, in some cases, eventual deposit in the Strategic National Stockpile. As background, in 2024, 40 institutions were awarded base contracts under the Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program. This program was a re-competition of her Animal Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program, and its overarching goal was to provide capability in a broad range of animal and animal replacement models for use in evaluating promising candidate countermeasures (vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics) against the broad range of infectious agents that are in the purview of DMID. The breadth of the existing contractor pool has enabled a rapid and effective response to emerging infectious diseases, such as COVID-19, and emergency preparedness priorities. Awarded contracts were divided into 4 model-specific pools: Task Area A � Small Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area B � Non-Human Primate Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area C � Animal Replacement and Non-traditional Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area D � Generation and Distribution of Specialized Reagents The Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases program will continue to provide the capability and capacity to develop and employ animal and animal replacement models (e.g., organ-on-a-chip technology) of infectious diseases for screening and product evaluation and addresses a critical stage in this pipeline by bridging in vitro testing and eventual clinical evaluation, including as needed, studies conducted under the guidance of 21 CFR 58, �Good Laboratory Practices�. In addition, for candidate products that are unable to be assessed for clinical efficacy in phase II or III trials for ethical or practical reasons, contracts awarded under this solicitation will enable regulatory approval or licensure via the guidance of the FDA�s Animal Efficacy Rule (21 CFR 314.610 and 601.91). This anticipated �ramp-on� solicitation will award multiple IDIQ base contracts to successful offerors that propose a general approach to the requirements, allowing them to join the existing contractor pools. Successful offerors will qualify for the pool and be eligible to compete for future task order awards in the existing model-specific Task Areas: Task Area A � Small Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area B � Non-Human Primate Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area C � Animal Replacement and Non-traditional Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area D � Generation and Distribution of Specialized Reagents Offerors are encouraged to consider submission of proposals to one or more of the above Task Areas (depending upon capabilities). Contract awards are anticipated to the organizations whose proposals offer the best value to the Government. For the purposes of this solicitation, the following definitions apply: Animal replacement tissue technologies derived from human or animal tissue (in particular lung, liver, immune system, brain, skin/soft tissue or gastrointestinal tissues): Organoids Organs on chips Artificial complex cell systems Microphysiological systems Tissue technologies derived from animals, in particular, non-human primates (for the purposes of bridging data from in vivo models with clinical data) Evaluation: encompasses advanced testing after a product has been screened and demonstrated as efficacious in the same or lower animal models; activities include dose refinement, measurement of host response, pharmacokinetics (in infected animals), pharmacodynamics (in infected animals), and therapeutic efficacy or immune protection against challenge. Model development: a novel systematic effort to reproduce a clinical syndrome caused by an infectious agent in an animal species following challenge with the agent and includes median lethal and/or infectious dose determination, natural history of infection, and serial pathogenesis studies. Model refinement: a systematic effort to improve the performance of an existing animal model that reproduces a clinical syndrome caused by an infectious agent; to adapt an existing animal model that reproduces a clinical syndrome caused by one infectious agent to a different, but related, infectious agent; to adapt an existing animal model to optimize its ability to support product screening or evaluation following challenge with the infectious agent. Non-human primate models: new and old-world species, including but not limited to Macaca, spp. (cynomolgus, Rhesus, pig-tailed); Chlorocebus, spp. (African green monkeys, vervets); Aotus, spp.; Papio, spp.; Callithrix, spp. (marmosets) Non-traditional animal models including but not limited to: Domestic livestock: horses, cattle, goats, sheep, fowl Wildlife species: marmots, wild rodents, deer, bats Invertebrates: snails, parasitic nematodes, parasitic protozoa, insect vectors of human disease Aquatic: zebrafish HFIM Pathogens: infectious bacteria, viruses, parasites, fungi, toxins, and other agents such as prions that cause clinical syndromes in humans (surrogate human pathog

title: NIH-31 Rodent Feed
description: Introduction This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice. Project requirements This specification is for the NIH-31 open formula, autoclavable rat and mouse ration containing 18% crude protein and void of any feed additives containing antibiotics or exogenous estrogens and certified limits on chemical and microbial contaminants as listed in the Statement of Work. Orders shall be placed according to the requirements of the Government, generally every 6 -8 weeks, as needed. Feed is ordered by tractor-trailer load of up to 1600 bags per shipment (80 bags/pallet, 20 pallets/truck load). Each bag contains 25-30 lbs. of feed. All feed must be milled within 6 weeks prior to the desired delivery date to allow time for testing and acceptance of the product. All lots of fishmeal must be pre-tested for Nitrosamines prior to milling the NIH-31 Rodent Diet to ensure the total concentration of N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) levels are at an acceptable concentration and do not exceed the MCL (10 ppb) for this product. Anticipated period of performance The Government anticipates awarding one firm fixed price, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity contract, featuring a one-year base period and four one-year option periods. The options periods may be unilaterally exercised by the Government. If the Government elects to exercise these options, the Contractor shall provide the resources as stated above. Capability Statements must not include links to internet web site addresses (URLs) or otherwise direct readers to alternate sources of information. Font size must be 10 to 12 points. Spacing must be no more than 15 characters per inch. Within a vertical inch, there must be no more than six lines of text. Print margins must be at least one inch on each edge of the paper. Print setup should be single sided on standard letter size paper (8.5 x 11" in the U.S., A4 in Europe). All proprietary information should be marked as such. Required Business Information: UEI. CAGE. Business size. SAM registration. Company Name. Company Address. Company Point of Contact, Phone and Email address Current contract vehicles, GSA Schedules, and/or Government-wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs) appropriate to this Sources Sought. Do you have a Government approved accounting system? If so, please identify the agency that approved the system. Type of Company (i.e., small business, 8(a), woman owned, veteran owned, etc.) as validated via the System for Award Management (SAM) located at https://sam.gov/content/home. This indication should be clearly marked on the first page of your Capability Statement (preferable placed under the eligible small business concern�s name and address). The email subject line must specify 75N98027R00023. Facsimile responses will not be accepted. CAPABILITY STATEMENTS RECEIVED AFTER THIS DATE AND TIME WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / MARKET SURVEY Project Title: Barrier IIB Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) System Replacement************** Procurement Identification: PANGLR -26 -034692**************NAICS Code: 238210 Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors (Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million)**************PSC Code: Z2BG Repair or Alteration of Electronic and Communications Facilities**************Estimated Project Magnitude / Cost: Between $250,000 and $500,000************** Primary Performance Location: Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal Electric Dispersal Barrier Facility (USGS / USACE Facility), 790 East Old Romeo Rd., Lockport/Romeoville, IL 60441*****************By way of this Market Survey/Sources Sought Notice, the USACE-Chicago District intends to determine the extent of firms that are engaged in providing the services described hereunder for the Barrier IIB Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) System Replacement. The responses to this Notice will be used for planning purposes for an upcoming procurement. Therefore, this Notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP); it does not guarantee the future issue of an RFP; nor does it commit the government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, this Agency will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that this Agency will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice; all costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the responding party expense.***************t this time, proprietary information is not being requested, and respondents shall refrain from providing proprietary information in response to this Notice. Responses to this Notice will not be returned. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this Notice.*******GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS Under the proposed contract, the contractor will be required to provide turnkey engineering, procurement, programming, fabrication, removal, installation, testing, and commissioning services for the controls modernization of the Barrier IIB Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) and Emergency Generator Paralleling Switchgear line-up (originally installed circa 2010).*********Scope Summary:************The project requires the complete replacement and modernization of obsolete proprietary electronic control modules, network processors, transducers, and human-machine interface (HMI) touchscreens with modern, open-architecture, commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) industrial control components.************The contractor shall provide a complete, non-proprietary functional solution meeting the following performance characteristics without relying on single-source, dealer-locked software or hardware:**************1. Master, Utility, Tie, and Generator Control Processors:************Furnish and program modular, open-architecture Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) or purpose-built Digital Generator Paralleling Controllers with industrial Ethernet communications.************** Provide dedicated processing hardware for:************* Master Switchgear Control (redundant processors AP1 and AP2)******** Generator Breaker Controls (dedicated controller per generator breaker)**********Utility Incoming Breaker Control (dedicated controller per utility breaker)*********Tie Breaker Control (dedicated controller per tie breaker)**********The control logic must automatically perform utility sensing, automatic transfer, generator start sequencing, dead-bus closing, auto-synchronization, isochronous kW and kVAR load sharing, soft-load open/closed-transition utility return, and load shed/add management.*********Programming must utilize non-proprietary, standard industrial software (e.g., standard IEC 61131-3 logic platforms).**************2. Power Sensing and Synchronization:********* Supply and install modern digital multi-function power transducers and automatic synchronizer / sync-check relays (Device 25) for each generator breaker, tie breaker, and utility source.*************3. Operator Interface (HMI) Visualization:***********Supply and install an industrial widescreen touchscreen display panel (minimum 15-inch diagonal) and dedicated processor running an industrial operating system.************The HMI software must display dynamic animated single-line electrical diagrams, breaker metering and status, alarm logging and management, mode selection (Auto/Manual/Test), and system diagnostics.***********Interface drivers must communicate natively via standard industrial protocols (Ethernet/IP, Modbus TCP, PROFINET, or OPC UA).**************4. Network and Communications:*********Furnish industrial managed Ethernet switches configured in a fault-tolerant ring communications architecture (replacing obsolete serial/proprietary network topologies).***********Provide protocol data gateways where necessary to output system data points (Modbus RTU/TCP or BACnet/Ethernet) to site supervisory networks.**************5. Simulation and Pre-Testing:***********All PLC and HMI programming must be factory bench-tested and verified using a static simulator reproducing the site sequence of operations prior to mobilization.**************6. On-Site Installation, Commissioning, and Constraints:************Perform on-site removal of legacy controllers, field wiring, mounting, terminations, calibrations, engine startup assistance, and full-load validation.************* Outage Limitation: On-site replacement and cutover must be accomplished within an aggressive coordinated window (estimated up to six (6) consecutive calendar days).************Life-Safety Operational Continuity: The Chicago Dispersal Barrier operates 24/7. During modernization, the emergency power system must remain functional such that at least one (1) emergency generator is continuously capable of automatic operation or rapid manual start to back up the site load.*************Deliver updated CAD as-built production drawings, sequence of operations manuals, bill of materials, component data sheets, and comprehensive on-site operator training.**********Estimated Period of Performance:********* Pre-engineering, hardware procurement, programming, and simulation testing: Ninety (90) to One Hundred Twenty (120) calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).**************On-site physical installation, cutover, testing, and training: Up to six (6) consecutive calendar days.**********REQUESTED INFORMATIONAL interested Small Businesses, certified HUBZone, 8(a), Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB), or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) should respond to this market survey/sources sought via email no via email no later than December 7, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Central Time.*************The following requests are designed to apprise the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Chicago District, of any prospective small business with industrial electrical switchgear, automatic transfer switch (ATS), and PLC control integration capabilities. title: P506 Pyro Equipment Procurement and Installation
description: The Department of War, Army Contracting Command - Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA), on behalf of Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought notice to conduct market research in accordance with FAR Part 10. The government is seeking to identify commercial vendors capable of providing, delivering, and installing specialized industrial manufacturing and energetics equipment. The purpose of this notice is to: - Identify qualified businesses (including Small Businesses, HUBZone, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, and Women-Owned Small Businesses) capable of fulfilling this requirement. - Gather industry feedback on the attached DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS) and equipment list (incorporated in the PWS). - Understand commercial manufacturing lead times, availability, and installation challenges for highly specialized pyrotechnic processing machinery to support FY27 procurement planning. **NOTE: This is a market research tool. This notice does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or quotes, and no contract will be awarded directly from this posting. SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT The contractor shall provide all management, tools, supplies, equipment, and labor necessary to procure, deliver, rig, and physically install specialized process equipment inside existing facility footprints at CAAA (Crane, IN). Because this machinery supports active pyrotechnics and explosive manufacturing operations, all applicable equipment and electronic controls must be rated Class 1 Div 1 (Groups C & D) and Class 2 Div 1 (Groups E, F, & G) or better. The primary equipment categories are detailed in the DRAFT PWS attached to this notice. **NOTE: This requirement is strictly for the procurement and physical installation of commercial industrial equipment into an existing facility footprint. Facility layout, floor plan design, and "brick-and-mortar" structural military construction (MILCON) are not within the scope of this vendor's effort. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors are requested to submit a brief Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages) in PDF format containing the following information: 1. COMPANY PROFILE -Company Name, Mailing Address, and Website - Unique Entity ID (UEI) and Cage Code - Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, and Email) - Active GSA Schedule Contract Number and relevant Special Item Number (SINs) (if applicable) 2. SOCIOECONOMIC & SIZE STANDARD - Business size standard under NAICS 333248 (or 333415) - Applicable socioeconomic designations (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB). 3. TECHNICAL CAPABILITY - A brief summary of your company's experience in sourcing, rigging, and installing heavy industrial machinery, air filtration, or chemical processing equipment within hazardous explosive-rated environments. 4. EQUIPMENT AVAILABILITY & LEAD TIMES - Review the attached PWS and identify which equipment items are standard "off-the-shelf" commercial products versus items requiring custom manufacturing or modifications - Provide estimated manufacturing and delivery lead times from date of contract award, noting any known supply chain bottlenecks that could affect FY27 execution. 5. DRAFT PWS FEEDBACK - Provide any industry questions, comments, or recommendations to clarify the requirements or remove restrictive language from the DRAFT PWS. IMPORTANT DISCLAIMERS In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. All information received in response to this RFI will be treated as information only, and the Government will not pay for any response preparation costs. All submissions must be sent via email to the following points of contact no later than Monday, December 7th, 2026, at 2:00PM CST: - Contract Specialist: Dustin Sexton (dustin.p.sexton.civ@army.mil)

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. title: C1AZ--631-21-011 Build Elevator Tower for Building 25 A/E Design SF330 Request for Qualifications
description: SPECIAL NOTICE FOR QUALIFICATIONS (SF 330) NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services (Small Business size standard $25.5M) A. INTRODUCTION: The VA Central Western Massachusetts Healthcare System (CWM HCS) plans to build and install a new elevator tower at Building 25 on the Leeds Campus. This project will correct a FCA deficiency. Provide all professional architectural and engineering (A/E) Part One Services (also known as Design Phase Type A & Type B Services) necessary to develop complete drawings, specifications, and cost estimates associated with building a new elevator tower at Building 25 and Part Two Services (also known as Construction Period Services Type C). The intent of this project includes but is not limited to: Evaluate existing elevator pit slab for buildings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 26 and design an elevator pit sump pump with oil interceptor. Design plumbing of oil water separator to sanitary sewer. See acceptable conceptual design attached. This conceptual design shall be validated. This shall be used to minimize and inform design efforts. Identify and address any issues or conflicts as necessary. If the elevator tower appearance is different than the conceptual design, conduct a Section 106 Historical Submission Report for VA to file with Massachusetts State Historical Preservation Office, by a Professional Historic Preservation Consultant. Existing report will be made available to the highest rated A/E firm. Conduct code compliance reviews (NFPA, ABAAS, VA Design Manuals, etc.) and integrate findings into design for compliance. Where conflicts exist between VA adopted codes and standards and the documents on the TIL, the A/E shall bring this to the attention of the VA. The resolution of the conflict shall be made by the authority having jurisdiction for VA to ensure consistency department wide. The A/E shall provide all services required to prepare documents and reports consistent with the VA s project team goals as prioritized during preliminary project meetings, field surveys and studies. The A/E shall determine existing conditions, severity of deficiencies, if any previous deficiencies have been corrected and to identify any conditions which may have previously been unreported. Cost estimates shall be prepared to reflect the cost of replacing the component in a standalone project (i.e., not as part of another project) and all costs including but not limited to asbestos removal if required, special field conditions and/or temporary equipment needed during the construction. Provide a Qualified Elevator Inspector during Construction Services to certify elevator. Also provide Part Two A/E Services (also known as Construction Period Services Type C) A/E Part Two Services of this design project (also known as Construction Period Services) includes responding to construction contractor Requests For Information (RFIs) during the solicitation (solicitation support) and construction phases of the construction project, attendance at post-award and commissioning kick off construction project conferences, review of construction material submittals and shop drawings, attendance at weekly teleconference construction meetings, approximately 1 site visits per month during active construction (both scheduled and emergent) to ensure compliance with the design drawings and specifications, preparation of site visit reports, coordination with project commissioning requirements/QEI inspection, review of any construction project modifications for cost and technical acceptability, attendance and participation during the pre-final inspection and final acceptance inspection, preparation of the punch list and preparation of record drawings of the completed construction project based on the construction contractor s as-built drawings. The A/E shall prepare a submittal log to be utilized by the VA during construction period services and maintain a RFI log. B. CONTRACT INFORMATION: The VA Medical Center Central Western Massachusetts located in Leeds, MA has a requirement for a Firm Fixed Price contract to provide professional A/E services for the 631-21-011 Building 25 Elevator Design project. The magnitude of construction is between $2,000,000 and $5,000,000. Prospective firms are reminded they must certify that in accordance with VAAR 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting-Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION), in the case of a contract for services (except construction), the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73 or certified VOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219- 74. Any work that a similarly situated certified SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractor further subcontracts will count towards the 50% subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. Other direct costs may be excluded to the extent they are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and small business concerns do not provide the service as set forth in 13 CFR 125.6. SF330 packages shall address how each firm anticipates meeting this criteria. This requirement is in accordance with the Selection of Architects and Engineers as implemented in Subpart 36.202 of the RFO and Subpart M836.102 of the VA Procurement Manual. All submissions will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation criteria. A "short list" of the three most highly rated after initial source selection will be chosen for negotiations of a contract award. The Government will not pay, nor reimburse, any costs associated with responding to this request. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. Respondents are put on notice that firm(s) selected by the Selection Authority will be required to submit a Fixed Price Proposal on the VA Form 6298 to include labor, overhead, profit, and other costs for this project for negotiation by the Contracting Officer prior to contract award. The negotiated agreement will be incorporated into the resulting contract. C. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL: This is a request for SF 330s only. Any requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. No material will be issued, and no solicitation package or bidder/plan holder list will be issued. D. PROJECT INFORMATION: Provide all professional architectural and engineering (A/E) services necessary to develop complete drawings, specifications, cost estimates, construction schedules, project phasing, investigations, site visits and construction period services associated with the 631-21-011 Building 25 Elevator Design at the VAMC Central Western Massachusetts HCS, Leeds, MA 01053. E. EVALUATION SELECTION CRITERIA: Each respondent s SF 330 submittal package will be evaluated in accordance with RFO 36.202 procedures. The selection criteria, in descending order of importance will be as follows: 1. Specialized Experience/Technical Competence 2. Professional Qualifications 3. Past Performance F. SELECTION CRITERIA DESCRIPTIONS: The selection criteria descriptions (1 through 3) are provided below in descending order of importance. Specialized Experience/Technical Competence Provide five (5) recent and relevant projects related to the Statement of Work with a similar magnitude (magnitude of construction for the design is between $2,000,000 and $5,000,000) that demonstrates experience with VA Design Requirements or equivalent with significant existing condition renovation. A minimum of three (3) projects should be for comprehensive designs of new elevator builds. Projects should detail the design manual requirements and required equipment for effective operation of an elevator, HVAC, and other necessary mechanical systems. Projects should also detail working with end users and reviewing manufacturer equipment. A minimum of two (2) projects should be for comprehensive design

title: US Embassy Quito RFQ for Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for qualified automotive service providers to perform preventive and corrective maintenance on Vehicles in Quito, Guayaquil, Manta and Machala.
description: The Embassy of the United States in Quito will establish Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for qualified automotive service providers to perform preventive and corrective maintenance on the U.S. Embassy�s Government-Owned Vehicles (GOVs), through directly owned facilities or qualified authorized partners in Quito, Guayaquil, Manta, and Machala, Ecuador. ensuring they remain safe, reliable, and mission-ready. The U.S. Government intends to award a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to one or more responsible companies submitting an acceptable quotation with fair and reasonable prices. We intend to award a BPA based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies if there is a need to do so. A BPA is an Agreement, not a contract, and neither party is bound by its terms and conditions. The Government is not obligated to purchase any definite amount under this BPA. If a need arises, an authorized representative of the Government may issue an order following the procedures outlined in the BPA. If the BPA-holder accepts the order, then a binding contract between the Government and BPA-holder will exist for that specific order. If the BPA-holder refuses to accept orders or furnish quotations in compliance with the terms of the Agreement, then it is likely that the Government will cancel the Agreement. Purpose and Scope The BPA intends to standardize maintenance services for a mixed fleet of Chevrolet, Dodge, Ford, Nissan, Renault, and other GOVs. It covers both preventive, mileage-based maintenance and corrective repairs for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles, with all work performed at the contractor�s licensed facility upon approval of quotations by the Procurement Section. Preventive Maintenance Program Preventive maintenance is structured around a detailed mileage-based schedule from 5,000 km up to 100,000 km. At lower mileage intervals, services focus on oil and filter changes, inspections (brakes, tires, belts, hoses, fluids, battery, underbody), and basic diagnostics. As mileage increases, additional tasks are added, including tire rotation and balancing, brake cleaning and fluid replacement, steering and suspension checks, cooling system tests and flushes, transmission and differential fluid services, fuel system cleaning, spark plug and fuel filter work, and timing belt inspections or replacement where required. Major services are defined at key intervals (e.g., 40,000 km, 50,000 km, 60,000 km, 80,000 km, 90,000 km, and 100,000 km) and include comprehensive diagnostics, safety inspections, and final reports. Corrective Maintenance Beyond scheduled maintenance, the contractor will provide corrective repairs as needed for major vehicle systems. This includes engine, transmission, brake, electrical, suspension, air conditioning, cooling, and exhaust system repairs, all performed only after submission and approval of written estimates. Parts, Standards, and Quality Assurance The contractor must use new OEM or equivalent-quality parts unless otherwise authorized, and work must be done by certified technicians in line with manufacturer recommendations and industry best practices. The Embassy retains the right to inspect completed work and require rework for any unsatisfactory services, ensuring consistent quality and compliance with the SOW. Administration, Reporting, and Warranty All services require prior authorization via approved quotations and purchase orders issued by the Procurement Section. The contractor must provide detailed service records, lists of replaced parts, and all relevant warranty documentation for each job. A minimum 90-day labor warranty is required on all work, along with the full manufacturer warranty on installed parts, providing post-service assurance and traceability for the Embassy. If you are interested in participating in this solicitation, follow the instructions in Section 3 of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit your proposal electronically to Quitoprocurement@state.gov referring to "Quotation Enclosed � Vehicle Maintenance Services". It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 25MB. If the file size should exceed 25MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 25MB each. before 16H00 on December 7, 2026. Direct any questions related to this RFQ to QuitoProcurement@state.gov In order for a proposal to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: 1. SF-1449 2. Section 1 Pricing 3. Section 5 Representations and Certifications 4. Additional information as required in Section 3

All other terms and conditions remain the same. ****************************************************************************************************************** Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (Fermilab) is soliciting proposals for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type Master Subcontract for Utilities Excavation and Repair Services for Fermilab located in Batavia, IL. Fermi Forward Discovery Group (FFDG) seeks to find a qualified subcontractor to perform on-call, scheduled, and emergency excavation services and utility repairs, as described in Exhibit C, Statement of Work, and the requirements of each task order. title: Notice of Intent - Sole Source - University Corporation for Advanced Internet Development, dba Internet2
description: The National Science Foundation intends to award a sole-source contract to University Corporation for Advanced Internet Development, dba Internet2 for Internet2 Non-Connected Affiliate Membership. The contemplated contract action is expected to result in a contract valued at approximately $39,861.00 and is anticipated to have a period of performance from 01/01/2027-12/31/2027. This notice is published in accordance with RFO FAR 5.101. Basis for Other Than Full and Open Competition The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source. The National Science Foundation has determined that Internet2 is the only source reasonably available capable of satisfying the Government's requirement because: Failure to renew Internet2 services would significantly impact NSF's ability to maintain connectivity with research and education networks that support critical agency programs and partnerships. Loss of access to Internet2 could disrupt data-sharing activities, research collaboration efforts, and network-dependent services relied upon by NSF staff, researchers, and external stakeholders. Transitioning to an alternative provider would require substantial planning, implementation, testing, and coordination efforts and could result in service interruptions, additional costs, and operational delays Renewing Internet2 support represents the most efficient, cost-effective, and lowest-risk approach to maintaining continuity of NSF's research network services. Continued use of Internet2 preserves established connectivity, operational stability, and interoperability with existing research and education partners while avoiding the technical and operational risks associated with migrating to a different solution. As a result, competition is lacking because no other known source can provide the required supplies or services within the Government's required timeframe and technical requirements. Interested Sources This notice is not a request for proposals. Nevertheless, any responsible source that believes it can satisfy the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating its ability to meet all requirements identified in this notice. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to the Point of Contact identified above no later than 4:00 PM EST, Monday, December 7, 2026. Responses will be evaluated solely to determine whether a bona fide competitive source exists for this requirement. Additional Information Intended Awardee: University Corporation for Advanced Internet Development, dba Internet2 Anticipated Award Date: 01/01/2027 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Place of Performance: 401 Dulany St., Alexandria, VA 22314 The Government reserves the right not to compete this requirement if no responses are received that clearly demonstrate an ability to satisfy the Government's requirement.

title: Repair and Maintenance of 10 Sprung Structures (8 WINMATs & 2 CRTFs) - Fort Wainwright, AK
description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION & SYNOPSIS: This announcement constitutes a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a separate written solicitation document will not be issued outside of the attached Request for Quotations (RFQ). Solicitation W912D027QA003 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) to establish a single, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) commercial services contract with an Over-and-Above (O&A) ordering mechanism. 2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, specialized tools, materials handling equipment (MHE) / aerial work platforms, freight/transportation, and OEM materials necessary to execute comprehensive structural, envelope, and architectural repairs to ten (10) government-owned, relocatable Sprung tensioned-membrane structures located within the cantonment area of Fort Wainwright, Alaska. Facility Breakdown: - Eight (8) Warm Maintenance Facility Shelters (WINMATs): RWS-01, RWS-02, RWS-03, RWS-04, RWS-07, RWS-08, RWS-09, and RWS-10 (Nominal Dimensions: 110 ft wide x 255 ft long; apex ridge height 35�45 ft). - Two (2) Combat Readiness Training Facility Shelters (CRTFs): CRTF-01 and CRTF-02 (Nominal Dimensions: 60 ft wide x 100 ft long). Core Scope Elements: - Architectural Membrane & Skin Restoration: Remediation of fabric punctures, tears, vestibule separations, and skirt damage utilizing manufacturer-specified hot-air extrusion or radio-frequency thermal welding. - Thermal Insulation & Vapor Barrier Repairs: Re-hanging, securing, and replacing dislodged interior R-30 insulation blankets and continuous poly vapor barrier films on end-walls and high ceilings. - Structural Tensioning & Hardware: Calibrated torque tensioning of structural bolts, replacement of broken arch spreaders, and reinforcement of structural anchoring assemblies. - Architectural Doors & Access: Mechanical overhaul, track realignment, and repair of 14' x 14' rolling overhead service doors, personnel man doors, panic hardware, and hinge weldments. - Ancillary Repairs: Exterior electrical outlet replacements and lightning protection grounding loop testing and repair. EXPLICIT SYSTEM EXCLUSIONS: Unlike previous regional temporary repairs, this contract strictly EXCLUDES maintenance, servicing, or repair of fuel-fired furnaces, unit heaters, fuel storage tanks, hydronic boiler systems, facility HVAC ductwork networks, fire suppression/sprinkler loops, or facility fire alarm/panel detection systems. 3. CONTRACT LINE ITEM STRUCTURE (CLIN): - CLIN 0001: Baseline Sprung Structure Repairs (8 WINMATs & 2 CRTFs) - Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) - CLIN 0002: Over-and-Above (O&A) Work Orders (DFARS 252.217-7028) - FFP Work Orders utilizing pre-priced labor rates (Government Not-to-Exceed Funded Ceiling: $125,690.00) 4. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: - Date of Contract Award (Anticipated 17 December 2026) through 31 January 2027. - Due to extreme sub-arctic winter weather in Interior Alaska, all on-site baseline repairs and exterior envelope welding must be 100% complete and accepted no later than 31 January 2027. 5. EVALUATION CRITERIA & BASIS OF AWARD: The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) offer. Source selection will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 12 and FAR Subpart 13.5 based on the following three evaluation factors: - Factor 1: Technical Capability (Subfactor 1A: Sprung OEM Preferred Contractor / Certified Installer Status; Subfactor 1B: Technical Execution Plan & Extreme Cold-Weather Methodology; Subfactor 1C: Schedule Compliance & 31 January 2027 Completion Commitment) - Factor 2: Past Performance (Evaluated as Acceptable, Unacceptable, or Neutral) - Factor 3: Total Evaluated Price (CLIN 0001 FFP + Evaluated CLIN 0002 Labor Formula [380 plug hours across 4 labor categories] + $125,690.00 O&A Materials Ceiling) Full evaluation details are set forth in Attachment 0007 (Evaluation Factors for Award - Addendum to FAR 52.212-2). 6. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS & PAGE LIMITS: Offerors must organize and submit quotes in three (3) distinct electronic volumes strictly in accordance with Attachment 0009 (Quote Submission Instructions - Tailored Addendum to FAR 52.212-1): - Volume I: Technical Capability (Maximum 15 pages, excluding OEM certificates and manufacturer authorization letters) - Volume II: Past Performance (Maximum of three (3) project references; maximum 2 pages per project). *Note on Local/Regional Offerors:* Given the specialized geographic market in Alaska, offerors are permitted to submit fewer than three references (e.g., one (1) or two (2) relevant projects). title: Risk Reduction support of future Avionics Management System (AMS) software builds
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Air Combat Electronics Program (PMA 209), Patuxent River, MD intends to negotiate and award a Delivery Order under Basic Ordering Agreement N0042126G1005, with Rockwell Collins, Inc., 400 Collins Road NE, Cedar Rapids, IA 52498-0505 to provide risk reduction activities in support of future Avionics Management System (AMS) software builds to include but not limited to engineering software development and testing, code enhancements and efficiencies, software prototyping and evaluation of new hardware, and conducting trade studies for best value design alternatives for future capabilities for the life cycle. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Rockwell Collins, Inc. is the original developer of the AMS and retains all data rights; making them the only company that has the ability, resources, technology, and documentation necessary to modify, develop, produce, maintain and support this system. THIS PRESOLICITATION NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPROSAL. The Government does not intend to fund the development or qualification of other sources for fulfilling this requirement. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability by responding to this requirement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this pre-solicitation notice. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No phone inquiries will be entertained. All inquiries and concerns shall be addressed via email to Bonnie Walsh no later than 7 December 2026, 4:30pm eastern time. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Rockwell Collins, Inc. directly.

description: Gesamtkonzept: Am Neufelder Weg 18 bis 20 in Schleswig befindet sich das Klinikgelände der Klinik für Forensische Psychiatrie. Die Klinik plant auf dem vorhandenen geschlossenen Klinikgelände u.a. den Neubau des Hauses 14. Das neue Haus 14 wird unmittelbar hinter dem Altbau entstehen. Für die Bauphase wird ein von der Klinik getrennter Baustellenbereich geschaffen. Übergangsweise wird für diese Baustelle eine eigene Zufahrt geschaffen. Der Neubau wird auf drei Geschossen insgesamt 60 Behandlungsplätze für Patient*innen des geschlossenen Maßregelvollzuges anbieten. description: Настоящата обществена поръчка съдържа класифицирана информация, представляваща държавна тайна по смисъла на Закона за защита на класифицираната информация (ЗЗКИ), поради което на основание чл. 172, ал. 3 от ЗОП възложителят поставя изисквания за защита на класифицираната информация при предоставяне на техническата спецификация на участниците и техните подизпълнители в процедурата и при сключването на договора. title: Finland – Emergency vehicles – Kahden tarkastusauton hankinta pelastuslaitokselle 2027, sisältäen optiot vuosille 2028-2029
description: Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta kahdesta (2 kpl) autoverovapaasta, paloautoksi katsastettavasta dieselkäyttöisestä ns. tarkastusautosta. description: Изпълнението на дейностите по поддръжка и ремонт изисква посещения и работа в обекти, свързани с отбраната и сигурността на Република България, с ниво на достъп до класифицирана информация „Секретно“, което налага поставянето на изисквания към кандидатите да притежават Удостоверение за сигурност на юридическото лице и Разрешение за достъп до класифицирана информация на физическите лица, съгласно на ЗЗКИ, с минимално ниво на достъп до класифицирана информация „Секретно“ или по-високо. title: Bulgaria – Repair and maintenance services of electrical building installations – „Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи запад“ ЕАД“, реф. № РРS 26-118
description: „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД провежда процедура от вида „договаряне с предварителна покана за участие“ с предмет: „Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи запад“ ЕАД“, реф. № РРS 26-118. Предметът на обществената поръчка е разделен на пет обособени позиции, както следва: Обособена позиция 1 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Изток 1, София Изток 2, Левски, Плевен извънградски, Видин-Белоградчик; Обособена позиция 2 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Север 1, София Север 2, Червен бряг, Бяла Слатина-Козлодуй, Ловеч, Троян-Тетевен, Перник-Брезник, Радомир; Обособена позиция 3 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Запад 1, София Запад 2, Монтана, Лом, Дупница, Кюстендил, сектор Параметризация, сектор СТИ; Обособена позиция 4 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: Враца, Мездра, Ботевград, Самоков-Костенец, Пирдоп, Сливница-Своге, Благоевград, Сандански-Петрич, Разлог, Гоце Делчев; Обособена позиция 5 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Юг 1, София Юг 2, Плевен град-Гулянци. Всеки кандидат/участник може да участва само за една обособена позиция при условие, че отговаря на изискванията на Закона за обществените поръчки (ЗОП), Правилника за прилагане на ЗОП (ППЗОП) и на изискванията на Възложителя, включително на критериите за подбор, посочени в обявлението и документацията за обществената поръчка. Критерият за възлагане на настоящата обществена поръчка при определяне на икономически най-изгодната оферта е „най-ниска цена”, определена съгласно методиката за оценка на офертите от документацията.

title: Design and construction of 5,964 SF addition to an existing aircraft paint shop and installation of a media blast booth
description: This project adds approximately 5,964 square feet (SF) of new preparation, administration, mechanical and decontamination spaces to the existing 4,818 SF Bldg 3035 Paint Shop. Installation of a Dry Media Blast Booth within the existing structure is also required. When completed, the 10,782 SF facility will contain strip and paint capabilities for an entire aircraft and its components, decontamination spaces for the Dry Media Blasting operations (as required by UFC 4-211-02), restrooms and other common support spaces (lactation, utility, and janitor�s closet). Minor renovation work and system replacements within the existing spaces will be required. Support facilities include: site development, utilities and connections, lighting, parking, walkways, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping, fire protection and alarm systems, energy monitoring control system (EMCS), Antiterrorism/Force Protection requirements, and sustainable/energy requirements. The Government has created a questionnaire/request for information (RFI) to capture industry responses to the above requirements. The link can be found in the attachments/links section of this special notice.

title: SOLICITATION NOTICE- Massena NY Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction
description: The purpose of Amendment #1 for the Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction solicitation is to extend the proposal due date from Saturday, November 21st, 2026 to Monday, December 7th, 2026 by 5:00pm EST and to include the attachment, "Site Visit Sign-In Sheet Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility." All proposals should be sent electronically via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov. All other terms and conditions remain the same. A forthcoming amendment will include responses to all RFIs received before the RFI deadline. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ Solicitation: Construction Services Contract for Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction project at the Massena LPOE, Rooseveltown, NY. Proposals are due Saturday, November 21st, 2026 by 5:00 pm EST. All proposals should be sent electronically via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov. The on-site visit will be held on Thursday, October 15th at 10am EST. All individuals who would like to attend must email kyle.cole@gsa.gov at least one day prior to the site visit to confirm their attendance. The site visit is not mandatory, but is encouraged. Questions are due via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov by close of business on Friday, October 30th, 2026. In order to receive the Specifications and Drawings for this solicitation, you must complete Attachment 10, "Safeguarding and Dissemination of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Building Information." The completed CUI Form must be sent via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov. Reference is made to the PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE Notice ID EQPXCAC-26-0011. All solicitation posts and updates for the Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction project will be posted to Solicitation No. 47PC5326R0029. Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction project at the Massena LPOE, Rooseveltown, NY includes, but is not limited to providing all labor, materials, tools, management, and full time on-site supervision required by contract documents to construct a Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility. The contract work incorporates site demolition/excavation/grading/planting/paving, general construction, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, hard-wall partitions, security, and telecommunication work to meet United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) requirements as follows: 1) Selective demolition of Architectural, Mechanical and Electrical systems, construction, and finishes at nearby Building G to support the renovation work. 2) Mechanical, plumbing, electrical, communication, security, and fire suppression systems to serve the uses of the new facility. 3) Earthwork, exterior improvements, and utilities for new facility. 4) Installation of common floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. 5) Installation of specialty floor, wall, and ceiling finishes as required. The contractor shall expect to interface with the GSA Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) for all major Life Safety contract submittal reviews and approvals. Typically, all submittals, once completed, will be grouped and transmitted to the AHJ for review and final approval. The contractor shall expect to interface with the US Customs and Border Protection agency representatives at the Land Port of Entry for all major submittal reviews and approvals as well as coordination for the installation of supporting equipment and devices with the facility. Exact work description will be identified and indicated in the Contract Documents. Products to be used will be specified within the drawings and individual Specification Sections. The contractor shall comply with the projects design specifications and drawings. The work will be constructed under a single prime contractor who is to adhere to all security requirements and guidelines for building access. The awardee will be required to complete the security clearance process. The procurement will be solicited and awarded to one (1) Total Small Business set-aside contractor. Offers from other than small business concerns will not be considered by the agency. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this procurement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business Administration standard of 45 million dollars in annual receipts averaged over the last three (3) completed fiscal years. This project shall be performed by an experienced Contractor that has performed similar work. The estimated performance period is 340 calendar days after Notice to Proceed has been issued. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The procurement method that will be implemented for this project will be in accordance with FAR Part 15.1-Source Selection Processes and Techniques. This project is a competitive acquisition utilizing the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) selection process. The government will evaluate technical responses using three evaluation factors to determine the proposal that best meets the requirements of the government. The vendor's experience, past performance, and staffing plan are acceptable/unacceptable factors. If a vendor does not meet the criteria for the prior experience factor, or the past performance, and receive an unacceptable, it will receive no further consideration under this acquisition. The vendor�s prior experience, past performance and staffing plan/structural organization factors, are equal in importance. All the technical evaluation factors, when combined, are significantly more important than price. This Contract will be awarded to a vendor whose proposal provides the lowest price with technically acceptable criteria to meet the government�s needs. The planned project delivery method will result in a Firm-Fixed-Price contract for construction services. Performance and payment bonds will be required following award pursuant to the Miller Act. A bid guarantee is also required. A description of GSA�s policies and procedures, in addition to that outlined in FAR 43.204, that apply to definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found at GSAM 552.243-71 Equitable Adjustments, https://www.acquisition.gov/gsam/552.243-71. Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM), in order to receive a contract award. Firms can register via the Internet site at https://www.sam.gov or by contacting SAM Service Desk at https://www.fsd.gov. The solicitation and associated information will only be available from the https://sam.gov website mentioned above. No telephone requests will be accepted. The solicitation will not be a sealed bid and there will not be a formal bid opening. All inquiries must be in writing, via email to the person(s) specified in the solicitation. All answers will be provided in writing and will be available on the aforementioned https://sam.gov posting. Offeror's will not be reimbursed for proposal submittal expenses. Several solicitation documents will be posted as "Locked" packages in the https://sam.gov posting. In order to view or download the packages, vendors must have a secure account. Information on how to register for an account and log in is available on the https://sam.gov website, under the "Getting Started" tab. Interested parties are strongly encouraged to register to this notice to receive notification of actions including posting of any amendments. However, offerors are advised to check the site frequently as they are responsible for obtaining amendments. DISCLAIMER: The official solicitation package and technical specifications will be located on the official Government web page and the Government is not liable for information furnished by any other source. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the https://sam.gov website for electronic downloading. This will normally be the only method of distributing

title: MetaSystems PMA
description: PLEASE READ THIS NOTICE CAREFULLY AS IT CONSTITUTES THE ONLY NOTICE THAT WILL BE PUBLISHED. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to MetaSystems Group, Inc., located at 200 Rivers Edge Drive, 1st Floor, Medford, MA 02155, for a base year with four (4) option years. The contract will provide preventive maintenance services and all software updates released during the period of performance. The FBI's Laboratory Division (LD) requires a maintenance service agreement for its MetaSystems Metafer5 Microscope systems. To maintain the manufacturer's warranty and ensure continued operational integrity of these critical instruments, maintenance and repair services must be performed by the original equipment manufacturer (OEM). The required maintenance agreement includes replacement parts, technical support, and software updates necessary to ensure the systems operate properly both as standalone instruments and as components of LD's integrated laboratory environment. Market research has determined that MetaSystems Group, Inc. is the only source capable of meeting the Government's requirements. MetaSystems does not authorize third-party vendors to perform maintenance, warranty, or repair services on its equipment. Any service performed by an unauthorized vendor would void the manufacturer's warranty. In addition, MetaSystems is the sole provider of support and maintenance for its proprietary software and does not provide software support to third-party service providers. As a result, MetaSystems service engineers are the only personnel qualified to provide the services required by the FBI's Laboratory Division. A Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC) is available upon request. This notice will be posted solely on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any updates related to this requirement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, and the applicable Product Service Code (PSC) is J066, Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment - Instruments and Laboratory Equipment. title: Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness and Validation Status
description: https://feedback.gsa.gov/jfe/form/SV_3t6dNlgkS4Vg6iy Federal agencies are preparing for the transition from cryptographic algorithms that may be vulnerable to future quantum computing attacks to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Public key cryptographic algorithms (i.e. asymmetric cryptography) currently used across Federal information systems, products and services � including Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman(ECDH), elliptic curve digital signature algorithms (ECDSA), and related mechanisms � will be vulnerable to a future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer (CRQC). As a result, Federal agencies are expected to identify, prioritize, and migrate quantum-vulnerable cryptographic systems to approved post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. Federal agencies are also required to use validated cryptographic algorithms and modules when cryptography is required to protect Federal information or Federal systems. The NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program establishes requirements under FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3. FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 requirements are applicable to U.S. Federal agencies when cryptographic-based security systems are used to provide information security for Federal operations and assets. If cryptography is required for the protection of information or data, then FIPS-validated cryptography is applicable. Non-validated cryptography shall be treated as providing no validated protection for Federal information where validated cryptography is required. Relevant policy, standards, and guidance include, but may not be limited to: NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program; FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules; FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard; FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard; FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard; NIST SP 800-208, Recommendation for Stateful Hash-Based Signature Schemes; NIST SP 800-52, Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of Transport Layer Security Implementations; OMB Memorandum M-22-09, Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles; Executive Order 14306, Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation�s Cybersecurity; Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks; OMB Memorandum M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography; and CISA guidance regarding product categories and technologies that use post-quantum cryptography standards. This RFI is intended to collect industry information regarding the availability, validation status, product and service readiness, procurement accessibility, implementation maturity, operational impacts, interoperability, and migration support associated with commercial products and services that support, or plan to support, NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography standards. This Request for Information is issued for market research purposes only. There are no anticipated tasks under this RFI. This RFI is intended to collect information from industry regarding vendor capabilities, products and services availability, cryptographic validation status, contract accessibility, and readiness to support the Federal Government�s migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or promise to issue a future solicitation. Any contract or order that may result from information received through this RFI will be subject to applicable procurement laws, regulations, and competition requirements. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred by industry in preparing or submitting responses to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the respondent�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation, if one is issued. title: RFI: Industry Interest in Use of NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Test Facilities and Capabilities
description: Public Notice/Announcement � Request for Information (RFI) THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Office of JPL Management and Oversight (NOJMO) to solicit responses from all interested parties. This document is for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to express interest in the use of NASA�s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) test facilities. This RFI is a standalone market research effort and is not related to, a continuation of, or a supplement to any previous RFI issued by NASA or NOJMO concerning the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), its facilities, capabilities, or potential industry use. This RFI is not related to any current or future competitive acquisition for the operation of the JPL. Responses to any prior RFI should not be considered responsive to this notice, and information submitted in response to a previous RFI does not constitute a response to this RFI. This notice is issued for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposals, or an offer or commitment by the Government to enter into a contract or other type of agreement. Purpose The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), a federally funded research and development center operated by the California Institute of Technology for NASA, maintains a broad portfolio of world-class facilities and test capabilities supporting spacecraft, instruments, robotics, and advanced technology development. NASA is conducting market research to assess industry interest in the potential short-term or medium-term utilization of select JPL facilities and capabilities. The purpose of this RFI is to: Understand potential demand for JPL test and integration facilities and services located in La Ca�ada Flintridge, California and other NASA-owned facilities managed or operated under JPL purview Inform internal planning related to facility utilization and potential access models Identify general categories of industry use cases and constraints Assess potential workforce, scheduling, and infrastructure considerations associated with external facility use In addition to facilities located at the primary JPL campus, certain capabilities may exist at associated NASA sites managed by JPL, including the Table Mountain Facility in Wrightwood, California, which supports optical communications, astronomy, and related technology demonstrations. Representative Facility Capabilities (see Attachment A) Representative Support Services (see Attachment A) Cost Recovery and Facility Use Considerations External use of NASA facilities is generally subject to cost recovery and usage fees consistent with federal policy governing the use of government-owned facilities and infrastructure. Depending on the nature of the activity, facility use may require reimbursement to NASA for costs including: facility operations and maintenance technical support services utilities and infrastructure usage scheduling and administrative support Specific cost structures or pricing models are not defined at this stage and may vary depending on the scope and duration of any future activities. Workforce and Staffing Considerations NASA is interested in understanding how potential industry users would envision staffing activities conducted within JPL facilities. Respondents are encouraged to address: Whether they anticipate bringing their own technical personnel to conduct testing or development activities within the facilities. The extent to which they may wish to leverage existing JPL or Caltech technical staff, engineering expertise, or operational support already available onsite.
